spec.title: Decisions
spec.description: OpenDT operates autonomously, yet a human can intervene and dictate major decisions; Automatic changes come from the self-calibrator, Manual ones from the operator. The dashed markers on the graphs show the same changes.

spec.title: Power [kW]
spec.description: The datacenter's telemetry on power draw (ground truth), OpenDT's prediction, and their gap, in the latest sample; below 0, OpenDT under-estimates.

spec.title: Jobs and hosts
spec.description: Few hosts in use means over-provisioning, where energy (and thus, money) is wasted by idle infrastructure. Many jobs waiting (a low share running) means under-provisioning, which could lead to performance concerns, system faults, and, ultimately, system failures.

spec.title: Sustainability
spec.description: The emission rate now and the grid carbon intensity it results from; the energy and the CO₂ over the selected interval (e.g., hour, day).

spec.title: Accuracy
spec.description: The lower the MAPE, the more accurate the prediction (red from 10%, the community-accepted error rate). The self-calibrator measures the difference between predictions and actual telemetry, then adjusts r, the calibration parameter of P(u) = P_idle + (P_max - P_idle)(2u - u^r), with u the CPU utilization.

spec.description: Ground truth alongside OpenDT's predictions. When the predicted curve closely tracks the ground truth, the twin accurately represents the physical infrastructure; when drift occurs, the operator can identify whether intervention is needed.
